jobs.title: AI Operations Manager
jobs.description: 🇪🇬 Up to EUR 25,000 per year, on a full-time, permanent employment contract 🌎 Fully remote working from anywhere in Egypt! 🏖️ 33 Days Paid Leave and Benefits ✨ Exciting high growth product, relied on by leading global brands, particularly within sports 💻 Working with the latest hardware, AI tools, and product workflows. About the Role We are hiring an AI Operations Manager to help drive the operational quality, reliability, and effectiveness of Storyteller’s AI tooling. This role sits within our AI Operations function and is focused on making sure the AI tools, platforms, workflows, and configurations used across the business are well-run, dependable, and continuously improving. AI is moving quickly, and Storyteller is moving with it. We need someone who can stay close to what is changing in the AI tooling landscape, understand what matters for our business, and help turn that understanding into practical operational improvements. A big part of this role is making sure AI tooling is configured properly, used effectively, and operating reliably. You will work with teams who use AI tools day to day, understand where tooling is creating friction, identify what needs to change, and follow through on the detailed operational work that makes systems dependable. This is a high-ownership role for someone who wants real responsibility for how AI tooling operates inside a fast-moving SaaS business. You will bring structure to messy tooling environments, improve visibility, support better standards, and help keep Storyteller in control of fast-changing AI platforms rather than reacting too late. This is not a passive maintenance role. It is for someone who likes improving systems, raising standards, and making AI tooling genuinely work better. About Storyteller Storyteller is a SaaS platform used by globally recognised brands across sport, media, entertainment, and beyond. Our platform helps companies create and deliver engaging story-style content experiences across their digital products. We work with high-profile clients, fast-moving teams, and products that are used by large audiences around the world. We are remote-first, product-led, and highly focused on execution. We care about clear communication, strong ownership, thoughtful use of technology, and building better ways of working as we grow. AI is already an important part of how our teams operate. The AI Operations function exists to make sure our AI tooling is reliable, well-configured, secure, useful, and continuously improving. This role is central to that work. What You Will Do Take operational ownership of the configuration, reliability, and standards of Storyteller’s AI tools and AI platforms. Support the AI Operations team’s response when AI tools, platforms, models, or underlying capabilities change. Set, maintain, and improve operational standards for how AI tooling is configured, accessed, used, and monitored. Improve visibility around AI tool configuration, platform usage, access administration, permissions, dependencies, and operational performance. Identify weak, unstable, or high-friction areas in our AI tooling setup and help develop practical solutions that are durable and scalable. Work with internal teams to understand where AI tooling is helping, where it is creating friction, and what needs to improve. Give leadership clearer visibility on where the AI tooling stack is performing well, where it is fragile, and what platform or workflow changes are needed next. Help ensure Storyteller’s AI tooling remains useful, controlled, reliable, and aligned with how the business actually works. What We Are Looking For Demonstrable experience managing or improving technical platforms, ideally including AI tools, automation platforms, LLM-based tools, or AI-enabled workflows. High agency and strong ownership of operational outcomes. Strong technical judgment, especially around AI tools, platform configuration, workflows, permissions, integrations, APIs, and dependencies.

jobs.title: Strengthening SUNCASA Evidence for GESI-Responsive Urban Nature-based Solutions:
jobs.description: Background The Scaling Urban Nature-based Solutions for Climate Adaptation in Sub-Saharan Africa (SUNCASA) project aims to enhance climate resilience, gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and biodiversity protection across three cities: Dire Dawa (Ethiopia), Kigali (Rwanda), and Johannesburg (South Africa). This initiative is led by the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) in partnership with the World Resources Institute, together with local partners. The main objective of SUNCASA is to address climate-induced risks (e.g., floods, landslides, and soil erosion) by implementing GESI-responsive nature-based solutions (NbS). This is aimed at strengthening the resilience of urban communities, watersheds, and biodiversity from the impacts of climate change, while reducing barriers to NbS participation among women and the underrepresented groups. This would be achieved through targeted interventions such as afforestation and reforestation programs, agroforestry, urban greening, and establishment of vegetated buffer zones in affected areas. The project was launched in late 2023, and implementation will be completed by late 2026. Despite growing interest and investment in urban NbS, relatively little evidence exists regarding how gender-responsive approaches to NbS influence project effectiveness, sustainability, governance, and equity outcomes. Gender-responsive approaches to NbS under SUNCASA are actions to protect, sustainably manage, and restore natural or modified ecosystems that address and challenge gender and social inequalities to promote equity, justice, and inclusion. This intersectional approach also considers diverse knowledge systems, including local knowledge, that result in equitable benefits from decision making and participation in NbS. As the project nears completion, SUNCASA offers a unique opportunity to strengthen the evidence base on how GESI-responsive NbS contribute to larger climate adaptation and biodiversity protection outcomes in urban contexts. To this end, IISD seeks to engage an external monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) consultancy team to conduct a theory-based end-of-project evaluation to assess progress toward achieving selected SUNCASA outcomes. The evaluation will employ theory-based mixed methods, such as key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) for different sets of actors from each city. Deliverables of this opportunity will include a final external evaluation report (reporting against select outcomes) and communications products to showcase SUNCASA’s early impact/outcomes. Given the short project timeline of 3 years, this evaluation will focus on assessing evidence that supports the pathways of change hypothesized by SUNCASA and early signs of impact and sustainability from the project rather than looking for long-term impacts or effectiveness. This RFP outlines the scope, objectives, and deliverables for engaging a MEL consultancy team for evaluation data collection and final deliverables. Objective of the Assignment This evaluation will assess the end-of-project progress toward achievement of selected SUNCASA intermediate and immediate outcomes that targeted decision-makers and local implementing partners participating in the project. Using mixed methods, a theory-based final evaluation report (including thematic case studies as part of the final report) will be developed to assess SUNCASA’s achievements in reaching selected outcomes. This assignment also requests an interim 2-pager communications product prepared to illustrate the early results and lessons from SUNCASA based on the evaluation, to support discussions at key events taking place in October/November 2026. Lastly, a shorter report will also be developed to showcase high-level results from the final report. Specifics regarding the assignment deliverables are provided in Section 3 of this RFP. jobs.title: Software Architect
jobs.description: Job Requisition ID # 26WD94957 Position Overview At Autodesk , we are pioneers in 3D design, engineering, and entertainment software, building tools that empower some of the most creative minds on the planet to solve real-world problems. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Glassdoor, and others as a top place to work, we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where innovation and creativity thrive. Autodesk 's Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) Data organization is seeking an experienced Software Architect to join the AEC Data team and define the cloud-native services and distributed-systems architecture that power the AEC Data Model (AECDM) and the many services around it. Data is the domain, but the role is fundamentally one of cloud and services architecture — APIs, service contracts, integrations, distributed-systems design, and the connected data model that ties them together — spanning multiple teams. It is not a data-warehouse or analytics-specialist role. The AEC Data organization is building the foundational data infrastructure behind Autodesk 's vision for connected construction: the platforms, services, and unified data models that span the entire built-asset lifecycle, from design and construction through operation and maintenance. This work enables the continuous flow of AEC data (3D models, 2D drawings, issue tracking, cost, sensor streams, and more) across Autodesk products and third-party integrations. The architect will help shape the next generation of capabilities for the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud, collaborating with software architects, domain experts, and product teams across Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, Autodesk Construction Cloud, and Autodesk Forma. This is a senior individual-contributor role on an established architecture track, reporting to the Distinguished Architect of the AEC Data team, who also serves as the Lead Software Architect. The primary responsibility is to shape how multiple teams design and build — through standards, reference architectures, ADRs, and design-review governance — rather than to own a single service. The exact focus flexes to your strengths and organizational need. Responsibilities API Design & Evolution : Design and evolve API surfaces across the AEC Data services — resource modeling, addressing, versioning and backward-compatible evolution, query APIs, and unifying overlapping surfaces into a single coherent contract. System Architecture : Define and evolve cross-team, cloud-native architecture across the AEC Data services; design distributed systems including service contracts and event-driven flows. Schema Design & Evolution : Design, document, and evolve data schemas for AEC domain entities (buildings, infrastructure, spaces, systems, components, relationships) — including semantic models, property sets, classification systems, and relationship hierarchies. Own versioning, backward/forward compatibility, deprecation, and migration; maintain the schema registry, validation rules, and quality checks. Standards & Governance : Establish standards, reference architectures, and reusable components; author architecture proposals and decision records (ADRs) for review by a cross-org architecture council, and run cross-team design reviews. Prototyping & Feasibility : Evaluate alternative architectural directions through modeling and prototyping, de-risking key decisions before broad adoption. Mentorship & Technical Leadership : Mentor engineers and fellow architects on emerging and established technologies and on architectural practice; grow technical depth across teams. Reliability & Performance : Ensure reliability, security, and performance of systems; define SLOs and drive observability (metrics, tracing, logging). Communication : Communicate architecture with clear views and diagrams (e.g., C4) and executive-ready narratives; produce comprehensive documentation and onboarding materials. jobs.title: Principal Full-Stack Engineer, Contract
jobs.description: Who Are We? Xcelirate develops technologically-advanced platforms which are accessed by thousands of users every minute! We are proud to offer a workplace where the sharpest developers come together to strategically plan and swiftly execute practices which see us maintain our existing market dominance and attain global expansion. We owe our success to our customers who have seen us grow across a decade, and our talented team who have made that growth possible. What are we looking for? You're a Principal-Level Full-Stack Engineer. You haven't just been around the block - you helped decide which blocks were worth building, and which ones should've been bulldozed early. At this point, programming languages don’t really impress you anymore. You treat them as tools that translate intent into something a compiler or interpreter can run, choosing them pragmatically, discarding them without nostalgia, and never confusing syntax or novelty with actual progress. You’ve been around long enough to remember when PHP constructors shared their class names, when exceptions were returned instead of thrown, and when Yeoman, Underscore, and CoffeeScript felt like the obvious future. More importantly, you also learned when to stop using those awful, awful, creations. Despite all that experience, you’ve stayed deeply hands-on, and you’ve never been particularly interested in drifting into management just because that seemed like the default next step. You’re still happiest close to the code. You bring a distinctly stoic approach to your work. You don’t panic when systems misbehave, you don’t chase drama, and you don’t confuse urgency with importance. When you join a project, things tend to settle down. Code becomes easier to reason about, systems start to feel calmer, and decisions get clearer. That sense of clarity tends to spread to the people around you, and without any formal mentoring process, they start picking things up simply by working alongside you. You have a solid, intuitive understanding of hot-path optimization, speculative execution, and lazy initialization, and you’re occasionally surprised that these simple concepts aren’t more widely understood. And the homelab experiments you keep running at home, purely because you’re curious and can’t help yourself? We definitely want to hear about those. If reading this feels a little too familiar, this role is likely to be a very good fit. What will you be doing? Manage your own time while adhering to priorities set by the company. Own complex engineering problems end-to-end, from problem framing and design through to delivery and iteration. Take responsibility for critical areas of the platform, ensuring they remain reliable, performant, and maintainable. Build new features and improve existing ones across our platforms. Refactor legacy and modern codebases pragmatically, balancing long-term health with delivery needs. Write tests (unit, integration, and end-to-end) to ensure software reliability. Be involved in every phase of the software lifecycle, from ideation to deployment. Participate in (and at times lead) deep technical discussions, helping drive sound decisions and trade-offs. Work hands-on across backend and frontend systems, stepping in wherever the problem lives. Identify inefficiencies and help streamline workflows, reducing unnecessary work. Collaborate closely with other senior engineers, raising the bar through example rather than authority Take ownership of your work, ensuring high-quality results and maintainable solutions.
